Observation: Top 20% of customers generated 59.3% of historical profit
Evidence: 397 customers; Gini (profit) 0.56; mean/median profit ratio 1.82; skewness 2.61
Business Interpretation: Customer value is concentrated: averages overstate the typical customer, so medians and percentiles are reported alongside means.

Observation: 52 high-value customers have not bought for >= 180 days
Evidence: They hold 5.1% of historical profit; median recency 228 days
Business Interpretation: Potentially at-risk, not churned: at the 2025 cutoff 56% of customers inactive >= 180 days bought again within 12 months.

Observation: Champions have the highest average estimated 12-month value (₹8,442), close to their historical annual rate (₹8,650)
Evidence: 334 customers = 50.8% of historical profit and 38.1% of estimated 12-month value
Business Interpretation: The segment that generated most past value is also estimated to generate the most near-term value. Its share is lower on the estimate partly because the model pulls extreme customers toward the average (test top decile: predicted ₹9,925 vs actual ₹11,090).

Observation: Can't Lose Them: estimated 12-month value is 0.72x their historical annual profit rate - the lowest ratio of any segment
Evidence: 79 customers; average historical profit ₹11,046; estimated ₹3,871 vs annual rate ₹5,411; average recency 228 days
Business Interpretation: Historical value alone would overstate what this group is estimated to contribute next year.

Observation: Clusters 0 and 2 hold 76.9% of estimated 12-month value
Evidence: Cluster 0 (High-Value, Active): 18.3% of customers, 52.9% of historical profit, 40.0% of estimated value; Cluster 2 (Mid-Value, Lapsing): 38.0% of customers, 35.6% of historical profit, 36.9% of estimated value
Business Interpretation: Cluster 0 has by far the highest value per customer (₹8,128 estimated); the lapsing mid-value cluster matters because of its size.

Observation: Cluster 1 (Low-Value, Active) has the highest estimated-to-historical ratio (1.68x)
Evidence: Average estimated 12-month value ₹2,621 vs historical annual rate ₹1,565; average tenure 14 months
Business Interpretation: Recently active, low-value customers are estimated to be worth more next year than their short history shows - partly model shrinkage toward the average, so treat as a ranking signal, not a forecast.

Observation: Longer-tenure customers have higher historical profit (Spearman 0.36)
Evidence: Median profit: tenure < 1 year ₹1,677, 1-2 years ₹4,068, >= 2 years ₹5,564; 38.7% of customers have left-censored tenure
Business Interpretation: Part of this is exposure (more time to buy), so tenure is not by itself evidence of loyalty.

Evidence: Median profit ₹735 vs ₹4,590 for repeat purchasers
Business Interpretation: Most value comes from repeat purchasing; a second purchase is the key step.

Evidence: Historical profit ₹1.40 Cr on revenue ₹6.01 Cr; 32 customers have negative total profit
Business Interpretation: Profit CLV is the more economically meaningful measure; revenue CLV is kept for comparison.

Observation: Out-of-time test (2024 features -> 2025 profit): R² 0.27, MAE ₹2,793
Evidence: Top 20% predicted captured 41.5% of actual 2025 profit; predicted/actual total 0.90; Spearman 0.49
Business Interpretation: Useful for ranking customers by expected value; individual rupee estimates are approximate and totals are conservative when activity grows.
